question_text: A 42-year-old man is brought to the emergency department by the police after he was involved in a physical altercation at a friend’s home. Upon physical examination, the patient is disheveled. He is very agitated and actively strikes out at nurses and other hospital staff. A decision is made to place him in restraints. Head, eyes, ears, nose, and throat exam reveals temporal wasting, marked tooth decay, and healing and new ulcers in his mouth and on his lips. His pupils are dilated and minimally reactive to light. His skin shows dramatic diaphoresis as well as excoriations over his arms. Vital signs show pulse of 120/min, respirations of 12/min, temperature of 39.0°C (102.2°F), and blood pressure of 150/100 mm Hg. Urine drug screen is positive for an amphetamine. Which of the following is a life-threatening complication of the toxicity seen in this patient?

                    ### Question
                    A 42-year-old man is brought to the emergency department by the police after he was involved in a physical altercation at a friend’s home. Upon physical examination, the patient is disheveled. He is very agitated and actively strikes out at nurses and other hospital staff. A decision is made to place him in restraints. Head, eyes, ears, nose, and throat exam reveals temporal wasting, marked tooth decay, and healing and new ulcers in his mouth and on his lips. His pupils are dilated and minimally reactive to light. Vital signs show pulse of 120/min, respirations of 12/min, temperature of 39.0°C (102.2°F), and blood pressure of 150/100 mm Hg. Urine drug screen is positive for an amphetamine. Which of the following is a life-threatening complication of the toxicity seen in this patient?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Heat stroke
opb. Malignant hyperthermia
opc. Respiratory depression
opd. Seizure
ope. Sudden cardiac arrest

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Amphetamine toxicity increases metabolic rate and stimulates the sympathetic and central nervous systems, leading to elevated body temperature and potential heat stroke, increased heart rate and blood pressure with a risk of sudden cardiac arrest, and neurological excitation that can cause seizures. Malignant hyperthermia and respiratory depression are less directly associated with amphetamine toxicity.
